'''Steve O'Shea''' (born 14 December 1965 in [[Auckland]], New Zealand)<ref>{{cite web |url=http://steveo-shea.webnode.com/about-us/ |title=About Me |author=Dr Steve O'Shea |access-date=22 November 2021}}</ref> is a [[Marine biology|marine biologist]] and [[environmentalist]] known for his research on [[giant squid]].<ref>{{cite magazine
 | url = http://www.newyorker.com/archive/2004/05/24/040524fa_fact1
 | title = The Squid Hunter
 | first = David | last=Grann
 | magazine = [[The New Yorker]]
 | date = 24 May 2004
| access-date = 20 October 2007
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
 | url = https://www.foxnews.com/story/giant-squid-finally-captured-on-film
 | title = Giant Squid Finally Captured on Film
 | publisher = [[Fox News]]
 | date = 28 September 2005
| access-date = 20 October 2007
}}</ref>

O'Shea obtained his degrees from Auckland university. He undertook a Bachelor of Science between 1984 and 1988. He graduated with an M.Sc. in 1990.<ref name="TONMO" /> The title of his 1998 doctoral thesis was ''New Zealand Octopoda (Mollusca: Cephalopoda) : systematics''.<ref>{{cite thesis |last=O'Shea |first=Steve |year=1998 |type=Doctoral thesis |title=New Zealand Octopoda (Mollusca: Cephalopoda) : systematics |publisher=ResearchSpace@Auckland, University of Auckland |hdl=2292/910}}</ref> He began work with the giant squid whilst working for the [[National Institute of Water and Atmospheric Research]] (NIWA) in [[New Zealand]] in 1996.<ref name=TONMO>{{cite web
 | url = http://www.tonmo.com/oshea.php 
 | title = Steve O'Shea Autobiography and Select Bibliography (2008)
 | publisher = TONMO.com
 | year = 2003
 | access-date = 20 October 2007 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170421103800/https://www.tonmo.com/pages/oshea/ |archive-date=21 April 2017
}}</ref> He became the Director of the Earth and Oceanic Sciences Research Institute at the [[Auckland University of Technology]] in 2005,<ref>{{cite news
 | url = https://www.usatoday.com/news/science/2003-04-03-squid_x.htm
 | title = Colossal squid caught in Antarctic waters
 | newspaper = [[USA Today]]
 | date = 4 March 2003
| access-date = 20 October 2007
}}</ref> and was a [[Discovery Channel]] Quest Scholar.<ref name=TONMO /> In 2009 he resigned from his Discovery Quest position to focus his research on coastal conservation, environmental matters and postgraduate supervision and teaching; despite this he has remained active in squid research, but is best known (in the popular press) for his involvement with large [[cephalopod]] [[taxon|taxa]], particularly [[giant squid|giant]] and [[colossal squid]]s, and their preservation. In 2011 he resigned from his position at the Auckland University of Technology.

O'Shea has published extensively on cephalopods, fisheries, whale diet and shallow subtidal coastal ecology.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://steveo-shea.webnode.com/my-publications/ |title=My publications |author=Dr Steve O'Shea |access-date=22 November 2021}}</ref> He lived in [[Sydney]] during the 2010s<ref>{{cite web
 | url = http://steveo-shea.webnode.com/
 | title = Dr Steve O'Shea
 | publisher = WEBNODE.com
 | year = 2012
 | access-date = 11 February 2013
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
 | url = http://www.photo-2-you.com//
 | title = Roving Photographer
 | publisher = WEBS.com
 | year = 2014
 | access-date = 17 June 2014
}}</ref>, and currently resides in [[Paris]], France where he runs a small editing business.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-04-10 |title=About DrO-editing: Dr Steve O'Shea |url=https://www.dro-editing.com/about/ |access-date=2026-06-11 |website=www.dro-editing.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Media appearances ==
O'Shea has appeared in over 13 documentaries on squid, whales and the oceans.<ref>{{cite web |url= http://steveo-shea.webnode.com/my-documentaries/ |title=My documentaries |author=Dr Steve O'Shea |access-date=22 November 2021}}</ref>

==Eponymy==
Six marine species have been named after O'Shea to honour his contribution to science:

*''[[Awhiowhio osheai]]'' (sponge)<ref>{{cite report |url=http://docs.niwa.co.nz/library/public/NIWAbm121.pdf |title=Porifera: Lithistid Demospongiae (Rock Sponges) |publisher=NIWA |year=2007 |first=Michelle |last=Kelly |pages=39–41}}</ref>
*''[[Brucerolis osheai]]'' (isopod)<ref>{{cite journal |title=New species of Brucerolis (Crustacea: Isopoda: Serolidae) from seas around New Zealand and Australia |url=https://museumsvictoria.com.au/collections-research/journals/memoirs-of-museum-victoria/volume-66-issue-1-2009/pages-147-173/ |journal=Memoirs of Museum Victoria |volume=66 |issue=1 |year=2009 |doi=10.24199/j.mmv.2009.66.15 |pages=147–173|doi-access=free }}</ref>
*''[[Calvetia osheai]]'' (bryozoan)<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1080/00288330.2003.9517196 | volume=37 | title=Endemic new cyclostome bryozoans from Spirits Bay, a New Zealand marine‐biodiversity "hotspot" | journal=New Zealand Journal of Marine and Freshwater Research | pages=653–669| year=2003 | last1=Taylor | first1=Paul D. | last2=Gordon | first2=Dennis P. | issue=3 | s2cid=83821530 | doi-access=free }}</ref>
*''[[Gonodactylellus osheai]]'' (mantis shrimp)<ref>{{Cite report |title=Mantis Shrimps (Crustacea: Stomatopoda) |url=https://docs.niwa.co.nz/library/public/Memoir%20125_The%20Marine%20Fauna%20of%20New%20Zealand_Mantis%20Shrimps.pdf |publisher=NIWA |first=Shane T. |last=Ahyong |pages=23–25 |year = 2012}}</ref>
*''[[Magnoteuthis osheai]]'' (squid)<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1080/03014223.2015.1063516 | volume=42 | title=Systematics of the Mastigoteuthidae Verrill, 1881 (Cephalopoda: Oegopsida) from New Zealand waters | journal=New Zealand Journal of Zoology | pages=187–256| year=2015 | last1=Braid | first1=HE | last2=Bolstad | first2=KSR | issue=3 | s2cid=86026467 | doi-access=free }}</ref>
*''[[Vulcanolepas osheai]]'' (deep-sea barnacle)<ref name=Buck2000>Buckeridge, J.S. 2000. ''Neolepas osheai'' sp. nov., a new deep‐sea vent barnacle (Cirripedia: Pedunculata) from the Brothers Caldera, south‐west Pacific Ocean, New Zealand Journal of Marine and Freshwater Research, 34:3, 409–418.</ref>
